newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says unaware of S.Africa Timor plan.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says unaware of S.Africa Timor plan.

text.p: Indonesia said on Thursday it was unaware of any initiative on East Timor being undertaken by South African President Nelson Mandela.

A senior official in Jakarta was commenting on reports that Mandela was reported to have invited prominent East Timorese exile and joint Nobel Peace Prize winner Jose Ramos Horta for a visit to Pretoria.

Mandela last week held a secret and highly unusual meeting with jailed Timorese rebel leader Xanana Gusmao while on a state visit to Indonesia that was attended by Indonesia's roving ambassador on East Timor, Lopez Da Cruz.
The Portuguese news agency Lusa reported from Lisbon on Thursday that Horta would leave for South Africa on Friday at the invitation of Mandela.
"I haven't heard anything about this," Da Cruz told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"The position of the South African government has been that they will give their support to tripartite talks between Portugal and Indonesia under the auspices of the United Nations," he said.

"For the time being, the international community is looking at the process, which is going on under the auspices of the U.N. secretary-general, to find a solution which will be judged to be comprehensive and internationally accepted," he said.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in late 1975, annexing the former Portuguese colony the following year, in an act that has not been recognised by the United Nations.
The United Nations regards Lisbon as the ruling power despite Jakarta having declared East Timor its 27th province.
A small band of armed guerrillas, led by Gusmao until his capture in 1992, and an overseas diplomatic effort led by Horta have opposed Jakarta's rule of the troubled territory for almost 22 years.
Last year, Horta and East Timorese Bishop Carlos Belo were jointly awarded the Nobel Peace Prize, raising the profile of the territory's troubles.
Da Cruz said he did not think Indonesia would have a problem with Mandela meeting Ramos Horta, depending on what came out of the meeting and what public statements were made.
"Mr. Mandela is an open-minded leader. The proof is that during the meeting with Xanana, I was there, too, and he was quite neutral in his comments," Da Cruz said.

Indonesian and Portuguese senior officials are due to meet on August 4, most probably at the United Nations in New York, to lay the groundwork for future ministerial meetings as part of the tripartite dialogue, he added.
